title: GDP and GNP

segments.say: An Indian company earns profits from a factory abroad. A foreign company earns profits from a factory in India. Which of these belongs in India's income?
Gross domestic product measures all the final goods and services produced within the country's borders in a year, whoever produces them.
Gross national product starts with GDP. It adds income that Indian-owned factors earn abroad, and subtracts what foreign-owned factors earn here.
So GDP asks where something was produced. GNP asks who produced it.
The difference has a name: net factor income from abroad. If Indians earn more abroad than foreigners earn here, GNP is bigger than GDP. If not, it is smaller.
Take away depreciation, the wear and tear on machines and buildings, and you get net national product.
For GS Three, remember: GDP asks where, GNP asks who, and net factor income from abroad is the bridge between them.

sources: NCERT Class 12, Introductory Macroeconomics, ch. 2 (National Income Accounting): GDP measures the aggregate production of final goods and services within the domestic economy in a year; GNP ≡ GDP + net factor income from abroad (factor income earned by domestic factors employed in the rest of the world minus factor income earned by foreign factors employed in the domestic economy); NNP ≡ GNP − depreciation

options: GDP plus net factor income from abroad
quiz.why: NCERT: GNP ≡ GDP + net factor income from abroad.

quiz.q: What do you subtract from GNP to get NNP?
Which measure counts output by where it is produced?
quiz.why: GDP covers production within the domestic economy.

reviewNote: All facts are from NCERT Class 12 Introductory Macroeconomics ch. 2. The opening uses company profits on purpose: money sent home by workers settled abroad is a transfer, not factor income, so it isn't used as an example. Moving facts: none (no figures quoted).
